mainTopic: The time limit for הפרת נדרים: the end of the day (תנא קמא) versus twenty-four hours (מעת לעת), the ruling against the twenty-four-hour pair, and how quickly חכמים released vows
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion. The רבנן usually do learn from a קל וחומר, but here the פסוק 'אישה יקימנו ואישה יפרנו' blocks it. Only a vow that could be confirmed (הקם) can be cancelled (הפר), so a husband cannot cancel a vow before it is made. A new משנה then teaches that a father or husband may cancel a vow 'all day', meaning until nightfall of the day he hears it. Depending on when the vow was made, that window can be long or very short. A ברייתא records רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who give a full twenty-four hours (מעת לעת). The גמרא shows that each side uses both פסוקים, 'ביום שמעו' and 'מיום אל יום', each in its own way. רבי יהושע בן לוי, and רב quoting his uncle, rule that the הלכה does not follow that pair. The amud ends with two short reports of חכמים who released vows brought before them very quickly.

steps.title: A verse limits cancelling to vows that could be confirmed
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן do use קל וחומר in general, but here the פסוק 'אישה יקימנו ואישה יפרנו' teaches that only a vow that could be confirmed can be cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, normally we do learn from a קל וחומר. But here it is different, because the פסוק says 'her husband may confirm it and her husband may cancel it.' This teaches that a vow that has reached the stage where it can be confirmed has also reached the stage where it can be cancelled. A vow that has not reached the stage where it can be confirmed has not reached the stage where it can be cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the earlier question of why the רבנן did not accept the קל וחומר. They agree that a קל וחומר is usually valid, but a פסוק overrides it in this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר would have let a husband cancel a vow ahead of time, before it was even made. The פסוק ties הפר to הקם: you can only cancel what you could also confirm. A vow that does not exist yet cannot be confirmed, so it cannot be cancelled either.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger one
Has come into the category of, has become eligible for

steps.whatToRemember: Only a vow that could be confirmed (הקם) can be cancelled (הפר). That is why a husband cannot cancel a vow before it is made.
steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן are not saying a קל וחומר is invalid in general. They agree it usually works. A specific פסוק blocks it here.

phrases.english: Yes, generally they do expound a kal vachomer,
but here it is different,
for the verse says:
"Her husband may confirm it, and her husband may cancel it."
That which has become eligible for confirming
has become eligible for cancelling;
that which has not become eligible for confirming
has not become eligible for cancelling.
phrases.notes: He means a vow she hasn't made yet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, בְּעָלְמָא דָּרְשִׁי קַל וָחוֹמֶר, וְשָׁאנֵי הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from before this section about why the רבנן reject the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A specific פסוק overrides a general method of learning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the רבנן accept קל וחומר, they should let a husband cancel a vow in advance.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק links הפר to הקם, so a vow that does not exist yet cannot be cancelled.

steps.title: The new משנה: cancelling is allowed all day
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that vows can be cancelled 'all day', and that this rule can work out both leniently and strictly.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Cancelling vows can be done all day. This rule can make things easier, and it can make things stricter.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a general rule about the time limit for cancelling vows. It also tells us the rule cuts both ways, setting up the examples that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'All day' means the father or husband has until the end of the calendar day on which he heard the vow. It is not a fixed number of hours. That is why it can sometimes give him a lot of time and sometimes very little.

keyTerms.meaning: All day, until the day ends
To be lenient and to be strict

phrases.english: MISHNA: The cancelling of vows is all day.
phrases.notes: He means the whole day on which he heard the vow.

phrases.english: There is in the matter a leniency and a stricture.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: the time limit for הפרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow may be cancelled until the end of the day on which it was heard.

steps.title: Examples of the lenient and strict outcomes
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives two examples. A vow on Friday night can be cancelled until שבת ends at dark. A vow made just before dark must be cancelled before nightfall.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If she vowed on Friday night, he may cancel on Friday night and all of שבת day until dark. If she vowed right before nightfall, he may cancel only until it gets dark. If it got dark and he had not cancelled, he can no longer cancel.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains its own rule with two examples. One shows the leniency (a long window) and one shows the stricture (a very short window).
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the Jewish calendar the day starts at night. A vow made on Friday night therefore gives almost a full day to cancel. A vow made just before dark gives only a few minutes, because the day ends at nightfall.

keyTerms.meaning: Friday night, the start of שבת

steps.confusionAlert: 'Night' here begins the day, so Friday night belongs to שבת. That is why the window runs until Saturday at dark.

phrases.english: How so?
If she vowed on Shabbat evening,
he may cancel on Shabbat evening
and on Shabbat day until it gets dark.
If she vowed as darkness was falling,
he may cancel only before it gets dark,
for if it got dark and he had not cancelled,
he can no longer cancel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the 'leniency and stricture' just mentioned in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The window to cancel ends at nightfall of the day the vow was heard, however long or short that leaves.

steps.title: A ברייתא: all day versus twenty-four hours
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא repeats 'all day', but רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון say the window is twenty-four hours from the time he heard the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in a ברייתא: Cancelling vows is all day. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון said: it is from time to time, a full twenty-four hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that some תנאים disagree with the משנה's rule. They hold the time limit is a full twenty-four hours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view (תנא קמא) counts by the calendar day, so the window can be very short. The second view counts twenty-four hours from when he heard the vow, so he always gets a full day.

keyTerms.meaning: From time to time, a full twenty-four-hour period

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a real disagreement about how to measure 'a day' for הפרה. The next steps look for the source of each view.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ תַּנְיָא: הֲפָרַת נְדָרִים כׇּל הַיּוֹם.
phrases.english: GEMARA: It is taught: The cancelling of vows is all day.
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda
and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon said:
From time to time.
phrases.notes: Twenty-four hours counted from the moment he heard the vow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that records a disagreement with the משנה's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: until the end of the day. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: a full twenty-four hours.

steps.title: What is the first view's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind the תנא קמא's 'all day' view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the first תנא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the first view gets its rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack. It is a request for the source. Once the source is clear, we can see why the two sides disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed תנא in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: What is the reason of the first tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first view in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for limiting הפרה to the calendar day.

steps.title: The source: 'on the day he hears'
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא learns from the פסוק 'ביום שמעו': cancelling is tied to the actual day he heard the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'on the day that he hears it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. The Torah says 'on the day', so the window ends when that day ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'day' (יום) is read as the calendar day, which ends at nightfall. That is exactly why a vow made just before dark leaves almost no time to cancel.
steps.whatToRemember: תנא קמא: 'ביום שמעו' means the calendar day, so cancelling ends at nightfall.

phrases.english: The verse says: "On the day that he hears."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'ביום שמעו' ties הפרה to the calendar day on which he heard the vow.

steps.title: What is the source for the twenty-four-hour view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning of the pair who say there are twenty-four hours to cancel.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what is their reason?
steps.whatsHappening: Having just given the reason for the תנא קמא, the גמרא now asks for the reason of the other side. This line sets up the next step, where the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'רבנן' means the two תנאים from the ברייתא, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. They allow twenty-four hours from when the vow was heard, so the גמרא wants to know which פסוק they rely on.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis. Here it refers to the pair of תנאים in the ברייתא

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, what is their reason?
phrases.notes: 'The Rabbis' here are the two תנאים from step 4, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel question: after the תנא קמא's source, the גמרא asks for the opposing view's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק supports the twenty-four-hour window.

steps.title: The source: 'from day to day'
steps.stepSummary: The twenty-four-hour view learns from the פסוק 'מיום אל יום'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is written: 'From day to day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this pair learns from the words 'מיום אל יום'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They read 'from day to day' as a stretch of time running from a given hour on one day to the same hour on the next day. That gives a full twenty-four hours counted from when he heard the vow, no matter when the calendar day ends.

keyTerms.meaning: From day to day. Read here as a full twenty-four-hour stretch

phrases.english: Because it is written: "From day to day."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'מיום אל יום' teaches a span from an hour on one day to the same hour on the next day.

steps.title: What does the first opinion do with 'from day to day'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the תנא קמא: the פסוק says 'מיום אל יום', so why not twenty-four hours?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the first תנא, isn't it written 'From day to day'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the תנא קמא with the other side's פסוק. If the Torah says 'from day to day', how can he limit the window to the calendar day?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides have a פסוק. The תנא קמא relies on 'ביום שמעו', but the Torah also says 'מיום אל יום', which seems to support twenty-four hours. The תנא קמא must explain what those words teach him.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא
But isn't it written...? Opens a challenge from a פסוק

phrases.english: And according to the first tanna,
isn't it written: "From day to day"?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְתַנָּא קַמָּא, הָא כְּתִיב ״מִיּוֹם אֶל יוֹם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the opposing side's source against the תנא קמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah also says 'מיום אל יום', which seems to give a twenty-four-hour window. That contradicts limiting cancellation to the calendar day.

steps.title: 'From day to day' teaches that night counts too
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא needs 'מיום אל יום' to teach that cancelling works at night, not just in daytime.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed. If the Torah only said 'on the day he hears', I would think daytime yes, nighttime no. So it says 'from day to day'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תנא קמא needs 'מיום אל יום' for something else. Without it, we might think the word 'day' means daytime only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ביום שמעו' alone could suggest he can only cancel during daylight. 'From day to day' teaches that the night between days is included, which fits the משנה's case of a vow heard on Friday night (step 3). So for the תנא קמא, these words add the night. They do not create a twenty-four-hour window.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed. The words teach something necessary
I would have thought. The mistaken first idea

steps.confusionAlert: For the תנא קמא, 'מיום אל יום' does NOT mean twenty-four hours. It only teaches that night is also a time when he may cancel, within the same calendar day.

phrases.english: It is necessary.
For if it said only "on the day he hears,"
I would have said: in the daytime, yes,
at night, no.
So it is written: "From day to day."

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the פסוק to a different teaching (צריכותא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From 'ביום שמעו' alone, cancelling would work only in daytime.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'מיום אל יום' includes the night, but the window still ends with the calendar day.

steps.title: What does the twenty-four-hour view do with 'on the day he hears'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the twenty-four-hour view with the פסוק 'ביום שמעו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says 'from day to day', isn't it written 'on the day he hears'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns the challenge around. The twenty-four-hour view must explain the words 'ביום שמעו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'On the day he hears' seems to tie cancelling to that one calendar day, which is the תנא קמא's view. The other side must show what these words teach them.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
On the day he hears it

phrases.english: And according to the one who says "from day to day,"
isn't it written: "On the day he hears"?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר ״מִיּוֹם אֶל יוֹם״, הָא כְּתִיב ״בְּיוֹם שׇׁמְעוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror of step 9, now aimed at the twenty-four-hour view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'ביום שמעו' seems to limit cancellation to the calendar day he heard the vow.

steps.title: 'On the day he hears' limits the window to one day
steps.stepSummary: The twenty-four-hour view needs 'ביום שמעו' so we do not stretch 'מיום אל יום' to a whole week.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed. If it only said 'from day to day', I would think he can cancel from one Sunday to the next Sunday. So it says 'on the day he hears'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the twenty-four-hour view needs 'ביום שמעו' to put a limit on 'מיום אל יום'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'From day to day' alone could mean from one day of the week to the same day next week, a full week. 'On the day he hears' limits it to the length of one day, which is twenty-four hours. Now both sides use both פסוקים, each in its own way.

keyTerms.meaning: From Sunday to Sunday, a whole week

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides use both פסוקים. For the תנא קמא, 'ביום שמעו' sets the calendar day and 'מיום אל יום' adds the night. For the twenty-four-hour view, 'מיום אל יום' sets the twenty-four hours and 'ביום שמעו' keeps it from becoming a week.

phrases.english: It is necessary, for if it wrote only "from day to day,"
I would have said: from Sunday
to the next Sunday he may cancel for her,
So it is written: "On the day he hears."

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the פסוק to a limiting role (צריכותא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מיום אל יום' alone could allow a whole week.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ביום שמעו' limits the window to one day's length, twenty-four hours.

steps.title: The הלכה does not follow the pair
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that the הלכה does not follow the twenty-four-hour pair.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן פזי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: The הלכה is not like that pair.
steps.whatsHappening: After both views have been explained, an אמורא gives the practical ruling: we do not follow the twenty-four-hour view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'That pair' means רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. So the הלכה follows the משנה: cancelling works only until the calendar day ends.

keyTerms.meaning: The pair. The two תנאים who said twenty-four hours

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical הלכה: a vow must be cancelled before the day ends, even if he heard it just before nightfall.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The halakha is not in accordance with that pair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the sources to deciding the practical הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows the משנה's 'all day' view, not the twenty-four-hour pair.

steps.title: רב stops לוי from following the pair
steps.stepSummary: לוי wanted to rule like the pair, but רב told him in his uncle's name that the הלכה is not like them.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי thought to act like those תנאים. רב said to him: This is what my uncle said: The הלכה is not like that pair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story that backs up the ruling. When לוי wanted to follow the pair in practice, רב told him not to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same ruling now comes from a second chain of teachers: רב, quoting his uncle. This confirms that in practice we do not give twenty-four hours.
steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכה: a vow can be cancelled only until the end of the day on which he heard it. We do not give a full twenty-four hours.

phrases.english: Levi thought to act in accordance with those tanna'im.
Rav said to him:
So said my uncle:
phrases.notes: רב calls his uncle רבי חייא 'חביבי'.

phrases.english: The halakha is not in accordance with that pair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 13's ruling with a practical story and a second chain of teachers.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, cancelling must happen before the day ends, not within twenty-four hours.

steps.title: חייא בר רב checks a vow as fast as shooting an arrow
steps.stepSummary: חייא בר רב would examine a vow in the time it takes to shoot an arrow. He handled it right away instead of making a long investigation.
steps.simpleTranslation: חייא בר רב would shoot an arrow and examine the vow at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how חייא בר רב handled a vow brought before him. He looked into it quickly, as if he were in the middle of shooting an arrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is about a חכם releasing (התרה) a vow brought before him. It is not the husband's or father's cancelling (הפרה) from the earlier steps. The arrow picture shows he did not sit down for a long, careful review; he released the vow right away.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a story about archery practice. The arrow is just a picture of how short a time he spent on the vow.

phrases.english: Chiyya bar Rav
would shoot an arrow and examine.
phrases.notes: He means he examined the vow while shooting, so it took him almost no time.

steps.triggerLanguage: חִיָּיא בַּר רַב שָׁדֵי גִּירָא וּבָדֵיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing the topic of the time limit for הפרה, the גמרא moves to a separate report about how a חכם acted when asked to release (התיר) a vow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חייא בר רב dealt with a vow immediately, without a lengthy examination.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא sits down and stands right back up
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא would sit down to look at a vow and stand up again right away. He also handled it quickly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא would sit and then stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, similar report. רבה בר רב הונא sat down to deal with a vow and got up again almost at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the report about חייא בר רב. Here the picture is sitting and standing instead of shooting an arrow. Both describe a חכם who did not spend a long time examining a vow.
steps.whatToRemember: Both חייא בר רב and רבה בר רב הונא handled vows brought before them quickly, without a long investigation.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna
would sit and stand.
phrases.notes: He would sit down to look at the vow and get right back up, so he barely stopped.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא יָתֵיב וְקָאֵים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second report, parallel to step 15, about another חכם who acted with the same speed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה בר רב הונא also dealt with a vow immediately, without a lengthy review.
